answer: An anti-Sybil check could rest on dawn lagoon wandering as proof of presence. Each applicant gets one stretch of lagoon shoreline and, on dates announced only hours ahead, must wander it at dawn, logging waterline markers and the drift of floating reeds. Tide and reed patterns change daily, so a scripted farm cannot precompute convincing logs, and one person cannot wander many distant shores at the same dawn. Local stewards verify logs against their own morning notes, so many fake identities would need many real early risers, while an honest participant walks a nearby shore.
